strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy/special hyperu(a,1,x) inaccuracy for small |a| and small x (gh-15650) on the buggy commit edff694ae469 by building SciPy from source and running the developer's added tests in scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py. The fix is a Cython-level change in _hypergeometric.pxd, so the extension must be rebuilt at each revision. Success is test_gh_15650_mp (and possibly test_gh_15650_sanity) failing on buggy and passing on fixed.

system_packages: C compiler (gcc or clang) with C++ and Fortran support as needed by SciPy's meson build
BLAS/LAPACK development libraries (e.g. OpenBLAS) if the build does not vendor them
git (to check out edff694ae469 and the fix commit)
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy && cd scipy && git checkout edff694ae469 && git submodule update --init
pip install -r requirements/build.txt (or the build/test deps listed in the repo)
spin build (rebuilds the Cython extensions; required again after checking out the fixed revision because _hypergeometric.pxd is included by the compiled module)

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py::test_gh_15650_mp (parametrized over 28 (a,b,x,expected) cases with b=1.0, a in about [-0.22,0.22], x in [1e-5,0.1]) and scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py::test_gh_15650_sanity (grid a in [-0.5,0.5], x in [1e-6,1e-1], asserting |result|<1e3)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision edff694ae469 with the test diff applied, test_gh_15650_mp fails for the small-|a| parametrizations because assert_allclose(sc.hyperu(a,1.0,x), expected, rtol=1e-13) exceeds tolerance; test_gh_15650_sanity may also fail if buggy values exceed 1e3. On the fixed revision (DLMF 13.3.7 branch applied for b==1, x<1, -0.25<a<0.3), all test_gh_15650 cases pass, so the transition is fail to pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: Evaluate sc.hyperu(0.1, 1.0, 0.01) and compare with mpmath.hyperu(0.1, 1, 0.01) at mp.workdps(100) on both revisions to confirm the buggy relative error before running pytest.
risks: The defect is only described for b==1 and small |a|, x; it is not shown to depend on platform, compiler, BLAS, or threading, so the transition is assumed to reproduce on a standard Linux x86_64 build. If the buggy path is architecture-dependent (e.g. only with certain libm exp/log implementations), the test may not fail on other platforms.
The fix edits Cython header _hypergeometric.pxd; a stale compiled extension will silently keep old behaviour, so a full rebuild between revisions is required to get a valid transition.

The patch condition is inconsistent in the evidence: applied diff uses -0.25<a<0.3, while the earlier discussion mentioned abs(a)<1 and abs(x)<1. The test points (|a|<=0.22) lie inside the applied region, so they are the decisive cases.
test_gh_15650_sanity only checks magnitude below 1e3 and may pass on the buggy revision even if test_gh_15650_mp fails; the transition should be judged on test_gh_15650_mp.
Buggy output values and error magnitude for a=0.1, x=0.01 are not given in the evidence; they are not invented here.

numpy is marked numerically_relevant false in the environment block but true in dependency_constraints; no version was documented or era-bounded, so no numpy version is pinned and the current compatible release for the checked-out SciPy tree is used.
mpmath is not imported by the added test; it is only used to generate the reference values, so it is listed for regenerating references, not as a runtime requirement.
Python version is not stated; use a version supported by the SciPy tree at edff694ae469 (the one that builds with its meson configuration).
The exact class name containing the new tests is not shown in the diff, so the test command selects by -k gh_15650 rather than a class path.

oracle.reference_source: mpmath mp.hyperu at mp.workdps(100), values hardcoded in test_gh_15650_mp
oracle.why: The developer test compares against 100-digit mpmath reference values with assert_allclose at rtol=1e-13, which is a relative tolerance check on the returned float.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On edff694ae469 the small-|a| cases in test_gh_15650_mp produce hyperu values that differ from the hardcoded references by more than rtol=1e-13, so assert_allclose raises AssertionError for those parametrizations; this is the expected failure path described in the issue as several-magnitude errors.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the DLMF 13.3.7 branch is used for b==1, x<1, -0.25<a<0.3, so the same parametrizations match the mpmath references within rtol=1e-13 and test_gh_15650_mp passes; test_gh_15650_sanity also passes because results are bounded.
